text:
Alex: heads-up — I'm seeing sustained memory climb on long Qwen-7B MQA sessions after warmstart. Not classic thrash/evict, looks like pages get reserved and never reused
Maya: which build/kernel? any change in kernel-selection heuristics lately?
Alex: prod-runtime@2026-03-17, kernel=auto (recently flipped to large-blocks for throughput). Rope scaling 2.1. Spike starts around 35–45k context then keeps a higher baseline.
Simon: could be fragmentation from large-block allocs + prefix prefetch. Did you profile kv page reuse vs reserve?
Alex: y, attaching short snippet from perf run:
```
kv_pages_allocated: 12432
kv_pages_evicted: 982
kv_page_reserve_count: 10320
kv_page_reuse_hits: 412
fragmentation_pct: 38.5
avg_pages_per_token_mqa: 0.0048
avg_pages_per_token_gqa: 0.0031
```
Alex: reuse hits are tiny relative to reserves, weirdly evicts are low.
Jess: infra-bot shows batch-priming enabled for that pool?
infra-bot: batch_priming=true pool=runtime-prod-1 deploy=2026-03-16T21:10Z
Maya: aha — batch priming can pre-populate longer prefixes for higher window ms. If kernel uses large-blocks that can create unusable internal holes.
Simon: also check coalesce frequency and GC sweep timer. If coalesce is deferred, lots of small free fragments accumulate inside large slabs.
Alex: did a quick A/B: disable priming -> memory drop ~22% at steady state, p50 latency +8% for long contexts.
Maya: tradeoff expected. Does the behavior differ for GQA?
Alex: yes — same test w/ GQA (same model family) shows ~10% steady memory bump instead of 22%. GQA seems to produce smaller page footprints so less fragmentation.
Simon: that matches internal expectations: MQA folds kv into denser blobs per head config so large-block kernels exacerbate.
Jess: can you share the perf flame for the reserve path?
Alex: clipped trace:
```
reserve_path -> prefetch_prefix (30ms window) -> kernel_alloc(large-block) -> page_link -> mark_pinned
evict_path rarely triggered
coalesce_task runs every 60s
```
Alex: notable: mark_pinned increments a refcount but we never clear when the prefetch window expires (race in batch priming cancel).
Maya: sounds like a bug in the cancellation path: prefetch requests that time out must unpin pages.
Simon: quick mitigation: bump coalesce frequency to 10s and force smaller kernel on pool to compact earlier. Longer term: fix prefetch cancel to decrement pin.
Alex: tried coalesce=10s + kernel=compact on a canary: memory baseline drops to expected and latency p95 back to nominal. Cost: throughput down ~6%.
Jess: do we have a regression test to catch re-reserve leaks on warmstart?
Maya: no deterministic one yet. We should add a long-context synthetic that does rope-scale >40k and asserts that reserve_count≈reuse_hits+evicts within tolerance after steady state.
Alex: filed INF-4827 with logs + repro script: https://redwood.inc/infra/INF-4827
Simon: I'll PR a quick hotfix to decrement pin on prefetch cancel and add the synthetic.
Jess: assign to @simon, add QA flag and note perf tradeoffs.
Alex: thanks — we'll keep priming off for that pool until patch lands. :thumbsup:
Maya: also note for releases: document model-specific guidance — MQA workloads likely want compact kernel or smaller block allocation for long contexts.
Alex: agreed. I'll add notes to the perf runbook.
Jess: nice find, nice repro, good call on canarying.
Alex: leaving the canary running, will post updated metrics later tonight.
